questions.q: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.why: He served from 1789 to 1797.

questions.q: In which year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.why: It was adopted on 4 July 1776.

questions.q: Which president issued the Emancipation Proclamation?
questions.why: He issued it in 1863, during the Civil War.

questions.q: Which ship carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620?
questions.why: They landed at Plymouth, Massachusetts.

questions.q: Who gave the 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963?
questions.why: He gave it at the March on Washington.

questions.q: Which attack in December 1941 brought the US into the Second World War?
questions.why: Japan attacked the naval base in Hawaii on 7 December 1941.

questions.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.why: He stepped onto the Moon during Apollo 11 in July 1969.

questions.q: From which country did the US buy Alaska in 1867?
questions.why: The price was $7.2 million.

questions.q: From which country did the US make the Louisiana Purchase in 1803?
questions.why: Napoleon sold the territory to raise money for his wars.

questions.q: Which amendment to the Constitution gave women the right to vote?
questions.why: It was ratified in 1920.

questions.q: Which president was elected four times?
questions.why: Presidents have been limited to two terms since 1951.

questions.q: The Civil War began in 1861 with an attack on which fort?
questions.why: It stands in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina.

questions.q: Who is the only US president to have resigned?
questions.why: He resigned in 1974 over the Watergate scandal.

questions.q: Which treaty ended the American Revolutionary War?
questions.why: It was signed in 1783.

questions.q: Who is called the 'Father of the Constitution'?
questions.why: He drafted much of it and the Bill of Rights.

questions.q: In which state was the Battle of Gettysburg fought?
questions.why: It was fought in July 1863.

questions.q: What is the capital of the United States?
questions.why: It has been the capital since 1800.

questions.q: Which is the largest US state by area?
questions.why: It is more than twice the size of Texas.

questions.q: Which US state is a chain of islands in the Pacific Ocean?
questions.why: It became the 50th state in 1959.

questions.q: Which river carved the Grand Canyon?
questions.why: It took millions of years.

questions.q: Which city is nicknamed 'The Big Apple'?
questions.why: The name was popularised by jazz musicians and a 1970s tourism campaign.

questions.q: In which state is Mount Rushmore?
questions.why: It is carved into the Black Hills.

questions.q: Which is the most populous US state?
questions.why: It has about 39 million people.

questions.q: Which is the only Great Lake entirely within the United States?
questions.why: The other four are shared with Canada.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain in North America?
questions.why: It rises to 6,190 m in Alaska.

questions.q: What is the capital of Texas?
questions.why: Houston is the largest city.

questions.q: What is the capital of California?
questions.why: It became the capital in 1854.

questions.q: Which became the world's first national park, in 1872?
questions.why: Most of it lies in Wyoming.

questions.q: Which is the smallest US state by area?
questions.why: It is under 4,000 square kilometres.

questions.q: How many US states border Canada?
questions.why: From Alaska and Washington to Maine.

questions.q: Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado meet at the Four Corners with which other state?
questions.why: It is the only point where four states meet.

questions.q: What is the capital of Alaska?
questions.why: It cannot be reached by road from the rest of the state.

questions.q: What is the NFL's championship game called?
questions.why: It is played every February.

questions.q: The World Series is the championship of which sport?
questions.why: It is played between the winners of the two major leagues.

questions.q: Michael Jordan won six NBA titles with which team?
questions.why: He won them in two runs of three, in the 1990s.

questions.q: Which trophy is awarded to the NHL champions?
questions.why: It is the oldest trophy in North American pro sport.

questions.q: Which swimmer won 23 Olympic gold medals?
questions.why: No other Olympian has won as many.

questions.q: Which gymnast has won the most World Championship medals in history?
questions.why: She has over 30 world medals.

questions.q: Which race is called 'The Greatest Spectacle in Racing'?
questions.why: It is run every Memorial Day weekend.

questions.q: Which boxer said 'Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'?
questions.why: He was a three-time heavyweight champion.

questions.q: Which quarterback won seven Super Bowls?
questions.why: Six with New England and one with Tampa Bay.

questions.q: Jackie Robinson broke baseball's colour barrier in 1947 with which team?
questions.why: Every MLB team now retires his number 42.

questions.q: Which horse race is the first leg of the Triple Crown?
questions.why: It is run at Churchill Downs every May.

questions.q: Jesse Owens won four gold medals at which Olympics?
questions.why: He won in front of Hitler's Germany.

questions.q: Which golf major is played every year at Augusta National?
questions.why: The winner receives a green jacket.

questions.q: Which NBA team won a record 18th championship in 2024?
questions.why: It took them one ahead of the Lakers.

questions.q: In the 1980 'Miracle on Ice', the US hockey team beat which country?
questions.why: A team of college players beat the Olympic champions in Lake Placid.

questions.q: Who scored 100 points in a single NBA game in 1962?
questions.why: Kobe Bryant's 81 is the next highest.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'King of Rock and Roll'?
questions.why: His home, Graceland, is in Memphis.

questions.q: Hollywood is a neighbourhood of which city?
questions.why: Film studios moved there in the 1910s.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'King of Pop'?
questions.why: His album 'Thriller' is the best-selling album ever.

questions.q: Which character first appeared in 'Steamboat Willie' in 1928?
questions.why: It was one of the first cartoons with synchronised sound.

questions.q: Which TV sitcom is set around the Central Perk coffee shop?
questions.why: It ran for ten seasons from 1994.

questions.q: Nashville, Tennessee, is famous for which kind of music?
questions.why: It is home to the Grand Ole Opry.

questions.q: Which city is called the birthplace of jazz?
questions.why: Jazz grew there around 1900.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Adventures of Tom Sawyer'?
questions.why: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens.

questions.q: Who wrote 'The Great Gatsby'?
questions.why: It was published in 1925.

questions.q: The Tony Awards honour the best in what?
questions.why: They are named after actress Antoinette Perry.

questions.q: Which singer is called the 'Queen of Soul'?
questions.why: Her hit 'Respect' came out in 1967.

questions.q: Which director made 'Jaws', 'E.T.' and 'Jurassic Park'?
questions.why: He has won three Oscars.

questions.q: What was Disney's first feature-length animated film, in 1937?
questions.a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
questions.why: Many called it 'Disney's Folly' before it became a hit.

questions.q: Lin-Manuel Miranda's musical 'Hamilton' is about which Founding Father?
questions.why: Hamilton was the first Secretary of the Treasury.

questions.q: Which poet wrote 'The Road Not Taken'?
questions.why: It was published in 1916.

questions.q: Which 1939 film was the first colour film to win the Oscar for Best Picture?
questions.why: It is still one of the highest-grossing films when adjusted for inflation.

questions.q: Which holiday falls on the fourth Thursday of November?
questions.why: It recalls a 1621 harvest feast at Plymouth.

questions.q: What is the traditional centrepiece of a Thanksgiving dinner?
questions.why: About 45 million turkeys are eaten each Thanksgiving.

questions.q: Which city is famous for deep-dish pizza?
questions.why: It is baked in a deep round pan.

questions.q: On what date is US Independence Day?
questions.why: It marks the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

questions.q: Which holiday is known for trick-or-treating?
questions.why: It is celebrated on 31 October.

questions.q: Which city is famous for its cheesesteak sandwich?
questions.why: It is made with thinly sliced beef and melted cheese.

questions.q: Gumbo and jambalaya come from which state?
questions.why: They come from Cajun and Creole cooking.

questions.q: Groundhog Day's most famous forecaster, Punxsutawney Phil, lives in which state?
questions.why: If he sees his shadow, six more weeks of winter are said to follow.

questions.q: Which celebration in New Orleans ends on 'Fat Tuesday'?
questions.why: Mardi Gras is French for 'Fat Tuesday'.

questions.q: Juneteenth marks the end of what in the United States?
questions.why: News of freedom reached Galveston, Texas, on 19 June 1865.

questions.q: Which state produces the most maple syrup in the US?
questions.why: It makes about half of all US maple syrup.

questions.q: Clam chowder is most associated with which region?
questions.why: New England chowder is creamy; Manhattan's is tomato-based.

questions.q: Which famous parade is held in New York City on Thanksgiving morning?
questions.why: It has been held since 1924.

questions.q: Which holiday on the last Monday in May honours those who died serving in the military?
questions.why: Veterans Day, in November, honours all who served.

questions.q: Which Texas city hosts the world's largest livestock show and rodeo?
questions.why: It draws over two million visitors each year.

questions.q: Key lime pie is the official pie of which state?
questions.why: It is named after the small limes of the Florida Keys.

questions.q: How many states make up the United States?
questions.why: Hawaii was the last to join, in 1959.

questions.q: How many stripes are on the US flag?
questions.why: They stand for the original 13 colonies.

questions.q: What is the national bird of the United States?
questions.why: It appears on the Great Seal.

questions.q: Where does the US President live and work?
questions.why: It is at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.

questions.q: Which famous monument was a gift from France?
questions.why: It was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.

questions.q: What is the national anthem of the United States?
questions.why: Francis Scott Key wrote the words in 1814.

questions.q: Which company did Steve Jobs co-found?
questions.why: He started it with Steve Wozniak in 1976.

questions.q: How many justices sit on the US Supreme Court?
questions.why: The number has been nine since 1869.

questions.q: How long is a US senator's term?
questions.why: A third of the Senate is elected every two years.

questions.q: In which state is NASA's Kennedy Space Center?
questions.why: Apollo 11 launched from there.

questions.q: Which inventor patented the phonograph in 1878?
questions.why: It was the first machine to record and play back sound.

questions.q: Near which town did the Wright brothers make the first powered flight in 1903?
questions.why: Kitty Hawk is in North Carolina.

questions.q: Which document begins with 'We the People'?
questions.why: It took effect in 1789.

questions.q: How many amendments make up the Bill of Rights?
questions.why: They were ratified in 1791.

questions.q: Whose portrait is on the $100 bill?
questions.why: He is one of two non-presidents on current US notes.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to become US President?
questions.why: Senators must be 30 and representatives 25.
